user.title: Log in to EZVIZ
user.description: Use the account that owns the doorbell. Logging in once registers this Home Assistant as one EZVIZ terminal.

code.title: Verification code
code.description: EZVIZ sent you a verification code. Enter it here.

devices.title: Choose your doorbell
devices.description: Select the door station. For an HP7 or CP7 this is the entry marked BDoorBell; if there is none, the one marked DBScreen. The indoor monitor is found automatically. Other EZVIZ cameras and doorbells of the account can be chosen too: they get events, pictures, recordings and live video, but no unlock buttons or chime controls (not tested on real hardware).

reauth_confirm.title: Log in again
reauth_confirm.description: The login for {username} no longer works. Enter the current password.

reconfigure.title: Change the EZVIZ login or doorbells
reconfigure.description: Account: {username}. Leave the password empty to keep the current one. The next step lets you choose the doorbells again.

error.invalid_auth: The account or password was not accepted.
error.invalid_code: The verification code was not accepted.

abort.already_configured: This account is already set up.
abort.no_devices: No devices were found on this account.

init.title: Options

data_description.poll_interval: How often EZVIZ is asked for new rings. Shorter means a quicker notification.
data_description.monitor_serials: Leave empty to find the monitor automatically. Otherwise list the serial numbers separated by commas (for a house with several monitors).

data.save_clips: Save the video of every ring
data.save_detection_pictures: Save the picture of every motion and person event in the media folder
data.motion_events: Motion as an event of the Doorbell entity
data.person_events: Person as an event of the Doorbell entity

data_description.save_clips: Off by default. After each ring the recording is fetched from the SD card and kept. A saved clip is announced by the event ezviz_instant_bell_clip_saved and the sensor Last saved clip. Needs an SD card in the door station and video encryption off; clips count towards the 500 MB the clip folder may use.
data_description.save_detection_pictures: Off by default. The pictures appear under Media > My media > ezviz_instant_bell, one folder per door station and day, about 5 to 12 seconds after the event; each one is announced by the event ezviz_instant_bell_picture_saved. Rings and door openings are not saved here. Which events the door station reports (motion, human detection) is set in the EZVIZ app.
data_description.detection_picture_days: Older day folders are deleted. Only the integration's own folder is touched.
data_description.motion_events: Off by default. The event entity then also fires motion, a few seconds after the door station reports it (it comes from the message list, like a ring). Which events the door station reports is set in the EZVIZ app.
data_description.person_events: Off by default. Like motion, for human detection. Motion and person are told apart by the name of the message; an unrecognised one stays Other.

data.stream_quality: Picture size of the local stream
data.wake_stream_minutes: Open the live video at a ring for (minutes)
data.keep_stream_open: Keep the live video open all the time

data_description.stream_source: cloud: through the EZVIZ relay. local: straight from the door station on your network, also when the EZVIZ cloud is down; Home Assistant must be on the same network. auto: local first, then cloud.
data_description.stream_mode: auto looks at the video once: H.264 uses the Home Assistant stream (sound, low delay), H.265 uses motion JPEG (every browser, no sound). webrtc and mjpeg force one of them.
data_description.video_codec: auto finds it out. h264 for H.264 firmware. hevc converts H.265 to H.264 for the Home Assistant stream; hevc_copy passes H.265 through unchanged (weak hosts, Frigate, Safari).
data_description.stream_quality: main: full size. sub: the door station's small picture, far cheaper to decode; use it if the video falls behind on a weak host such as a Raspberry Pi. Only for the local source.
data_description.encryption_key: Only needed when the door station encrypts its video and the key cannot be fetched from EZVIZ (see the repair notice or the action fetch_encryption_key). Usually the 6-character verification code on the door station's label. It decrypts the video of both sources.
data_description.wake_stream_minutes: 0 = off. At a ring (and at motion or a person, if those events are on) the live video is opened at once and kept open this long, so it shows without waiting when you look. Works with every source; through the cloud it uses upload while it is open.
data_description.keep_stream_open: Off by default. The live video then stays open day and night, like Frigate keeps it, and shows at once. Only works with the source local; with cloud or auto it is ignored, because the video would be uploaded to EZVIZ all the time. Costs some CPU in Home Assistant, more when the video is encrypted.

data.share_stream: Let other apps read the live video (go2rtc, Frigate)

data_description.share_stream: Off by default. Other apps then read the live video from the addresses above, through Home Assistant's web server: the first one is MPEG-TS with sound, the second motion JPEG. Anyone with an address can watch, so keep it like a password. A wrong token counts as a failed login. Reading an address opens the live video, like opening the Live camera.
data_description.new_stream_token: The addresses handed out so far stop working; the new ones are shown the next time you open these options.
data_description.relay_port: 0 picks a free port at each start. A fixed port is only needed to read the relay socket from another machine.
data_description.relay_bind: 127.0.0.1 (the default) keeps the relay on this computer. 0.0.0.0 lets other machines read the relay socket on the fixed port, without a password; a repair notice warns while it is set. The addresses with a token are the safer way.

data.aggressive_mpegts: Repeat the stream headers before every keyframe

data_description.aggressive_mpegts: Switch it on if the log shows 'Immediate exit requested'. Off by default.
data_description.diagnostic_dumps: Writes the start of the stream to two .bin files in the config folder, for a video bug report. Leave it off otherwise.

serial_needed.message: More than one doorbell is set up: give the serial number.

history_failed.message: Could not read the event list from EZVIZ: {error}

recordings_failed.message: Could not read the recordings of the SD card from EZVIZ: {error}

cloud_unreachable.message: EZVIZ cannot be reached right now, so this needs to wait. The local live video still works.

terminals_almost_full.title: EZVIZ terminal slots almost used up
terminals_almost_full.description: {count} of {limit} terminals are registered on this EZVIZ account. When all are used, new logins fail. Open the EZVIZ app, go to your account's logged-in devices and remove the ones you no longer use.

hevc_webrtc.title: HEVC live view on WebRTC mode
hevc_webrtc.description:
Doorbell {serial} streams HEVC/H.265, but Stream mode is set to WebRTC. Browsers can't show HEVC over WebRTC and go2rtc must transcode, which fails on weak hosts (grey screen or 'connection refused').

Open Configure on the integration and set Stream mode to 'mjpeg' (codec-agnostic, no go2rtc), then Reload. Alternatively, to keep WebRTC, set Video codec to 'hevc' to transcode to H.264.

stream_encrypted.title: Device is encrypting the video stream
stream_encrypted.description:
Doorbell {serial} is scrambling the video stream (Image/Video Encryption is on). The container stays readable but the payloads are scrambled, so ffmpeg cannot decode and the live view stays black.

Open the EZVIZ app → the device → Settings → **Image/Video Encryption** and turn it off (it asks for the 6-letter device code). Note: a firmware or app update can silently re-enable it.

confirm.title: Enter the code EZVIZ e-mailed you
confirm.description:
Doorbell {serial} encrypts its video, and EZVIZ has just e-mailed a 4-digit security code (subject "[Device Encryption] Security Code") to your account address. That code unlocks the stream, and it expires after about 30 minutes.

Enter it below. Do **not** use the 6-character code printed on the device label — this firmware rejects it. Submitting an empty field asks EZVIZ for a fresh code.

error.invalid_code: EZVIZ did not accept that code. It has probably expired — submit an empty field to have a new one sent.
error.resent: A new code has been sent. Check your e-mail and enter it here.

abort.no_device: That doorbell is no longer set up in Home Assistant.

cloud_offline.title: EZVIZ cannot be reached ({title})
cloud_offline.description: EZVIZ did not answer when Home Assistant started, so this integration runs with the local connection only: the local live video works with the stored key, while rings, unlocking, settings, recordings and pictures wait for the cloud. A new login is tried every 5 minutes, and everything starts again by itself when EZVIZ answers. If this stays, check the internet connection of Home Assistant.

open_relay.title: The live video relay is open to your network
open_relay.description: In the options of {title}, the **Relay listen host** is `{host}`. The relay has no password, so anyone who can reach this address can watch the live video of your door station. go2rtc and Frigate can read it through Home Assistant with a token instead: in the options under *Other apps*, switch on **Let other apps read the live video (go2rtc, Frigate)** and set the listen host back to `127.0.0.1`. This notice disappears when the relay listens on this computer only.

serial.description: Serial number of the doorbell. Optional when only one is set up.

set_video_encryption.name: Set video encryption
set_video_encryption.description: Turn the door station's Image/Video Encryption on or off. While it is on, the live video needs the camera key (see fetch_encryption_key) and the recordings of the SD card cannot be played. This changes a security setting of the device.

serial.name: Serial number
serial.description: Serial number of the doorbell. Optional when only one is set up.

enable.name: Encryption on
enable.description: On to enable encryption, off to disable it.

verification_code.name: Verification code
verification_code.description: The 6-character code on the device label, or the short code EZVIZ e-mails on newer firmware.

fetch_encryption_key.name: Fetch encryption key
fetch_encryption_key.description: Get the key that decrypts the video of an encrypted doorbell. Call once without a code (EZVIZ e-mails a one-time code), then again with the code.

serial.name: Door station
serial.description: Serial of the door station. Needed when the account has more than one.

code.name: Code
code.description: The 4-digit code from the e-mail. Leave empty to have one sent.
